item.title: PLA sends group to coordinate rescue efforts in mudslide-hit county in SW China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
CHENGDU, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- A directing group from the Western Theater Command of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) has been dispatched to the Xizang Autonomous Region in southwest China on Thursday morning to coordinate joint rescue operations by military personnel in mudslide-hit Gyirong County. Carried by the Y-20 transport aircraft of the western theater command, the group will organize military forces to assist in disaster relief efforts. The mudslide, which occurred on Wednesday, has resulted in three people dead and 265 missing in Gyirong, according to initial estimates.

item.title: Xi to attend SCO summit, pay state visit to Kyrgyzstan, Egypt
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- From August 30 to September 3, Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 in Bishkek, and pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt upon the invitation of President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan and President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi of Egypt, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Wednesday.

item.title: Xi urges all-out rescue, relief efforts after mudslide hits border port in Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missing after a mudslide in Nepal caused casualties at Gyirong border port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Wednesday morning. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called for efforts to evacuate residents at risk and provide timely medical treatment to the injured to minimize casualties. He made the instructions after a mudslide occurred at around 10:30 a.m. on Wednesday in Nepal, which caused severe casualties and left people unaccounted for at Gyirong border port in Gyirong County. Xi also stressed the need to strengthen monitoring and early warning, ensure scientific rescue operations and guard against secondary disasters. Noting that China is currently in a critical period of flood control, he urged local authorities and relevant departments to prepare for worst-case scenarios and extreme situations, fully implement measures for flood and typhoon prevention, and step up efforts to identify and address potential risks and hazards. He demanded resolute action to prevent major and catastrophic disasters and accidents and safeguard people's lives and property. Premier Li Qiang also issued instructions, calling for an immediate verification of the number of the missing and affected people and for all-out rescue and relief efforts. Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, instructed the Foreign Ministry to strengthen communication and coordination with relevant countries, promptly share information and work together to properly handle rescue and relief efforts. Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, led officials from relevant departments to the site to guide rescue and disaster-response operations. Authorities in Xizang have mobilized forces to carry out search and rescue operations. All relevant operations are underway.

item.title: China warns against unilateral sanctions after U.S. vows "economic asphyxiation" of Iran
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- China has made clear on multiple occasions that it firmly opposes illegal unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and are not authorized by the UN Security Council, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said on Tuesday. Lin made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on media reports that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, expanding Washington's secondary sanctions threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign. Economic warfare and maximum pressure do not help solve problems. Instead, they only escalate tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks, disrupt the global economic and financial order, and undermine the legitimate rights and interests of other countries, Lin said. The pressing priority now is to de-escalate the situation and return to the track of dialogue and negotiation as soon as possible, he added. China's cooperation with Iran is always conducted within the framework of international law and should not be disrupted or undermined, Lin said. China is closely following relevant developments and will take all necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests, he noted.

item.title: Chinese FM calls on Middle East, Gulf parties to resume dialogue, negotiation
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, holds talks with Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kuwait, in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 24. 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei) BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday that the current situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region is once again at a critical juncture, expressing hope that the parties concerned will return to the track of dialogue and negotiation as soon as possible. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when holding talks with Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, minister of foreign affairs of Kuwait, in Beijing. Wang added the top priority is to de-escalate the situation. Wang said China always attaches great importance to its relations with Kuwait and stands ready to take the 55th anniversary of the establishment of bilateral ties as an opportunity to build a China-Kuwait strategic partnership with a more solid foundation, higher-quality outcomes and greater substance. Wang also expressed confidence that Kuwait will continue to support China's just position on issues concerning its core interests and ensure the safety of Chinese personnel, institutions and projects in Kuwait. Jarrah said Kuwait sincerely appreciates China's long-standing selfless assistance and support for Kuwait in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity. Kuwait firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is ready to work with China to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state, Jarrah added. Jarrah noted that Kuwait stands ready to strengthen communication and coordination with China to promote the early restoration of security and stability in the Middle East and the Gulf region, and safeguard the freedom and safety of international waterways. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, holds talks with Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kuwait, in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 24. 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei)

item.title: Y-20 Taxies for Takeoff at Dusk
item.description:

A Y-20 long-range strategic heavy-lift transport aircraft attached to the Chinese PLA Air Force taxies on the runway under a golden sky during a training exercise on August 3, 2026. The Y-20 is China's first domestically developed new-generation large military transport aircraft. Characterized by long range, heavy payload capacity and high speed, it is capable of conducting long-distance airlift operations for both personnel and cargo under complex meteorological conditions.
